mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 5% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals a strengthening supply side, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO YoY growth exceeds 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is above 4% and CPIAUCSL is increasing, yet S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, leading to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS decreases by more than 100,000 and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% YoY and retail sales (RSAFS) are stagnant or declining, it signals a weakening demand side, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY decline > 10% and RSAFS stagnant/declining
failure_condition: If HOUST declines by more than 10% YoY and RSAFS is stagnant or declining, yet S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals accommodative monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and investment, which boosts corporate earnings and results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is below 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
